statement.p: Fabrienne is paying a dinner bill of {\$23.00}. Fabrienne plans to pay 20\% in tips. How much in total (including bill and tip) will Fabrienne pay?
Fabrienne will pay in total (including bill and tip).

solution.p: First, we need to find how much tip Fabrienne paid. This problem can be boiled down to this question: What is 20\% of 23? We will show multiple methods to solve this problem.
We will use proportion to solve this problem. Assume 20\% of 23 is x, so 20 out of 100 corresponds to x out of 23.
We will write and solve the proportion:
Fabrienne will pay {\$4.60} in tip. In total, she will pay {\$23.00}+{\$4.60}={\$27.60}.
Fabrienne will pay {\$27.60} in total (including bill and tip).
We will use the percentage formula to solve this problem. This translation from English to math may help you remember the percentage formula.
The question is: What is 20\% of 23? Assume x is 20\% of 23. We have:
Fabrienne will pay {\$4.60} in tip. In total, she will pay {\$23.00}+{\$4.60}={\$27.60}.
Fabrienne will pay {\$27.60} in total (including bill and tip).

li.p: 23 is the base (following the word of).

solution.p: By the formula \text{percentage} = \text{rate} \cdot \text{base}, we do a multiplication to solve the problem:
Fabrienne will pay {\$4.60} in tip. In total, she will pay {\$23.00}+{\$4.60}={\$27.60}.
Fabrienne will pay {\$27.60} in total (including bill and tip).
